AgentCardConfig.description:
Agent identity and capabilities advertised via the A2A Agent Card.

This interface captures all fields that appear in the public-facing agent card served at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. Orchestrators and callers use this metadata to discover the agent's name, supported modes, streaming capability, and available skills.

description.description: Agent description shown to orchestrators and callers. Should concisely explain the agent's purpose and domain expertise.

name.description: Human-readable agent name. Displayed in orchestrator UIs and agent discovery listings.

protocolVersion.deprecated:
Superseded by A2A v1.0's per-interface `protocolVersion`
(see `AgentCard.supportedInterfaces[]`, built by `buildAgentCard`).
Kept for backward compatibility with existing config files only —
the agent card builder no longer reads this value.
protocolVersion.description: A2A protocol version this agent supports.

provider.description: Agent provider information. Identifies the organization responsible for this agent deployment.

url.description: Optional URL for the provider's website or documentation.

pushNotifications.description: Whether the agent supports push notifications.

signing.description: Optional Signed Agent Card support (A2A v1.0, JWS per RFC 7515). Off by default. When enabled, the private key is read from the environment variable named by `privateKeyJwkEnvVar`, whose value must be a JSON-serialized JWK — never store key material in the config file itself.

keyId.description: Key ID (`kid`) to embed in the JWS protected header.

privateKeyJwkEnvVar.description: Name of the env var holding the signing private key as a JSON JWK.

skills.description: Skills this agent exposes to callers. Each skill represents a discrete capability advertised in the agent card.

stateTransitionHistory.deprecated:
This capability is not implemented in the A2A v1.0 spec and
was removed. Kept for backward compatibility only — value is ignored.
The agent card builder always sets this to `false`.
stateTransitionHistory.description: Enable state transition history capability advertisement.

streaming.description: Whether the agent supports streaming responses.

AgentConfig.description:
Complete agent configuration.

This is what a JSON config file (e.g. `agents/example/config.json`) maps to. All fields are optional — sensible defaults are applied for everything.

configDir.description: Directory containing the agent's config.json file. Populated automatically by the CLI scaffold when a config file path is provided. Used by the materializer for resolving relative paths in memory config.

customAgents.description: Custom agent definitions to register with Copilot sessions.

events.description: Event transport configuration for sideband observability events.

interactions.description: Whether a person is asked when Copilot wants to run a command, write a file or call a tool (permission requests) or asks a question (`ask_user`), and for how long. The default (`mode: "auto"`, no rules) is the headless behaviour this wrapper has always had: nobody is asked and every permission is approved. With `mode: "ask"`, what no `autoAnswer` rule answers reaches the A2A client as `input-required` and the task resumes on the reply.

mcp.description: MCP servers to connect via Copilot SDK at session creation. Keys are server names, values are server configs.

memory.description: Optional memory configuration for persisting instructions and skills. When present, the materializer writes these to backend-specific paths in the workspace directory during executor initialization.

otel.description: Wrapper-level OTel + Copilot Hook F only (`otel.backend.copilot`).

subAgents.description:
Optional sub-agents to expose as MCP tools via the `a2a-mcp-skillmap` bridge. When present, the parent agent spawns skillmap as a stdio MCP server and registers it under the reserved `a2a-subagents` key in the resolved  {@link  mcp }  map. Sub-agents declared here become callable as ordinary MCP tools by the Copilot SDK runtime.

When this field is absent or `agents` is empty, the parent skips every sub-agent code path with no side effects.

AzureProviderOptions.description: Azure-specific provider options. Only relevant when `type` is "azure".

CopilotConfig.description: How the wrapper connects to and interacts with GitHub Copilot SDK.

cliUrl.description: External Copilot CLI server URL (e.g. "localhost:4321"). If set, the SDK connects to this pre-running CLI server instead of managing its own CLI process.

contextFile.description: Filename for the pre-built domain context file in the workspace directory. Default: "context.md"

contextPrompt.description: Default prompt sent to build the domain context file. The LLM will write its findings to the contextFile.

githubToken.description: GitHub Personal Access Token for authentication. Required in Docker containers where `gh` CLI is not available. Maps to the SDK's `githubToken` option.

provider.description:
Custom LLM provider configuration (BYOK — Bring Your Own Key).

When set, bypasses GitHub Copilot and connects directly to the specified provider. Supports Ollama (local), OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, vLLM, LiteLLM, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Omit this field entirely to use the default GitHub Copilot API.

Note: when provider is set, the `model` field is REQUIRED — the SDK cannot auto-detect models from custom providers.

streaming.description: Enable streaming by default on sessions (default: true)

systemPrompt.description: System prompt prepended to the first message of every session. Use this to give the LLM its persona, role, and behavioral rules.

systemPromptMode.description:
How the system prompt is applied to the SDK-managed system message.

- "append" (default): your prompt is appended after the SDK's built-in   system message. The SDK's coding-assistant persona remains active.   Safe choice when you want to add constraints without replacing the base.

- "replace": your prompt completely replaces the SDK's system message.   A production-ready preamble is automatically prepended to instruct the   model to act as a deployed agent (no tool disclosure, no internal detail   leakage). Use this when you need a clean, custom persona.

workspaceDirectory.description: Working directory for context file operations

CustomAgentConfig.description: A custom agent definition passed to the Copilot SDK session.

EventsConfig.description:
Event transport configuration for sideband observability events.

Controls how trace events (MCP tool calls, agent reasoning, lifecycle) are delivered. Only the two built-in transports are configurable via JSON config — for custom transports (Kafka, Redis, DB, etc.), use the programmatic API and pass a transport function to `createA2AServer()`.

httpHeaders.description: Custom HTTP headers sent with every event POST. Values support `${VAR}` environment substitution (an unset variable is left as written and a warning naming the variable is printed once). Useful for authentication tokens: ```json { "Authorization": "Bearer ${CORTEX_TOKEN}" } ```

httpTimeout.description: HTTP request timeout in milliseconds for the `"http"` transport.

httpUrl.description: HTTP endpoint URL for the `"http"` and `"both"` transports. Required for those transports. Supports `${VAR}` environment substitution. Environment override: `A2A_EVENTS_HTTP_URL`.

transport.description:
Built-in transport type.

- `"a2a"` — publish as sideband trace artifacts on the A2A   ExecutionEventBus (default, zero dependencies).
- `"http"` — POST events as JSON to  {@link  httpUrl } .
- `"both"` — do both. The A2A artifact and the HTTP POST carry the same   `eventId`, so consumers can de-duplicate.

Environment override: `A2A_EVENTS_TRANSPORT`.

For custom transports, leave this unset and provide a transport function via the programmatic `createA2AServer()` API.

streamArtifactChunks.description: Stream artifact chunks individually (A2A spec-correct) vs buffer and send single artifact (inspector-compatible). Default: false (buffered).

InteractionsConfig.description:
Whether a person is asked when the backend wants to do something that needs a decision (a permission, a question) and what happens when nobody answers. Read by a wrapper that implements the provider contract and handed to the run runtime (`RunRegistryOptions.interactionPolicy`).

The default (`mode: "auto"`, no rules) keeps each wrapper's native behaviour and asks nobody.

authTimeoutMs.description: Ask mode: expiry of a sign-in (`auth`) interaction, in ms.

autoAnswer.description: Rules that answer without a person, first match wins, in both modes. A rule is `{ match: { kind?, risk?, tool?, action? }, answer: { kind } | { optionId } | { decline: true } }`; an empty `match` matches everything. Only option-based interactions (permission, confirm) can be answered by a rule.

mode.description: `"auto"`: nobody is asked; a rule in  {@link  autoAnswer }  answers what it matches and the wrapper's native handling applies to the rest. `"ask"`: what no rule answers goes to the A2A client as `input-required` and the task waits for its reply.

onTimeout.description: What an expiry does: `"fail"` fails the task; `"deny"` lets the run go on with the request denied (never approved).

timeoutMs.description: Ask mode: how long an unanswered interaction waits before it expires, in ms (30 minutes for sign-in).

McpHttpServerConfig.description: Configuration for an MCP server connected via HTTP (streamable).

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers sent with every request to this server. Use for auth tokens, API keys, etc. Values support `${ENV_VAR}` (or `$ENV_VAR`) substitution so secrets stay out of config.json — e.g. `{ "Authorization": "Bearer ${LINEAR_API_KEY}" }`.

url.description: URL of the remote MCP server (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8002/mcp)

McpSseServerConfig.description: Configuration for an MCP server connected via SSE.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers sent with every request to this server. Use for auth tokens, API keys, etc. Values support `${ENV_VAR}` (or `$ENV_VAR`) substitution so secrets stay out of config.json — e.g. `{ "Authorization": "Bearer ${NOTION_TOKEN}" }`.

url.description: URL of the SSE MCP server endpoint (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8001/sse)

McpStdioServerConfig.description: Configuration for a stdio-based MCP server.

args.description: Arguments to pass to the command. Values support `${ENV_VAR}` (or `$ENV_VAR`) substitution.

command.description: Command to launch the MCP server

env.description: Environment variables for the spawned process. Values support `${ENV_VAR}` (or `$ENV_VAR`) substitution so secrets stay out of config.json — e.g. `{ "API_KEY": "${MY_API_KEY}" }`.

MemoryConfig.description:
Optional memory configuration section in agent config.json.

Declares instructions and skills to materialize into the agent's workspace at startup. Both fields are optional — operators can declare instructions only, skills only, or both.

Paths are resolved relative to the directory containing config.json (Config_Directory) unless they are absolute.

instructions.description: Path to a markdown instructions file. Resolved relative to Config_Directory when relative, used as-is when absolute.

skills.description: Paths to skill directories, each containing a SKILL.md file. Resolved relative to Config_Directory when relative, used as-is when absolute.

OtelCopilotBackendConfig.description: Copilot CLI OTel knobs (only meaningful on `a2a-copilot`).

propagateTraceContext.default: true when Copilot OTel is configured

OtelCopilotConfig.description: `a2a-copilot` agent `otel` — common + Copilot Hook F only.

annotateUsageCalls.description: Emit per-LLM-call span **events** (`a2a.llm.call`) on the task span when the wrapper is the sole OTel token source. Off by default (noisy).

compat.description:
Opt-in platform compatibility attributes, added next to the standard ones (never replacing them). Default: none.

- `"langfuse"`: `langfuse.observation.type` (`agent` on the request span,   `tool` on mirrored tool spans) so Langfuse draws its agent graph.
- `"openinference"`: `openinference.span.kind` (`AGENT` / `TOOL`),   `agent.name`, `graph.node.*` (parent edge only when a parent agent is   known) so Phoenix shows agent icons and a graph.

Environment override: `A2A_OTEL_COMPAT` (comma-separated, `none` clears).

emitOverlappingBackendSpans.description: Unsafe escape hatch: allow wrapper tool/LLM spans even when backend OTel is configured (duplicates Copilot/Claude tool spans in the collector).

enabled.description: Master switch for wrapper-owned OTel instrumentation.

exporter.description: Shared OTLP exporter hint for wrapper hosts and backend passthrough. Backends inherit `endpoint` / `protocol` when their own fields are omitted.

headers.description: Extra OTLP request headers (e.g. Langfuse / Grafana Cloud Basic auth). Values support `${VAR}` environment substitution and are never logged. The standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` environment variable also works and is preferred when you want to keep secrets out of config files.

protocol.description:
OTLP encoding for CLI bootstrap.
- `http/protobuf` (default) — `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-proto`   (Phoenix accepts only protobuf over HTTP)
- `http/json` — `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http`

mirrorAgentEvents.description: When true, map `AgentEvent` tool calls into wrapper OTel child spans. Defaults to false. Forced off when a backend OTel block is present unless  {@link  emitOverlappingBackendSpans }  is true.

propagation.description: How an inbound W3C trace context (from the caller) is handled. See docs/design/distributed-tracing.md (sections 8.2 and 8.3). Environment overrides: `A2A_OTEL_INBOUND`, `A2A_OTEL_TRUSTED_PEERS`, `A2A_OTEL_UNTRUSTED`, `A2A_OTEL_CARRIERS`.

serviceName.default: derived from agent card / wrapper name
serviceName.description: Service name resource attribute for wrapper spans.

span.description: How the request span relates to an existing server span. Environment overrides: `A2A_OTEL_SERVER_SPAN`, `A2A_OTEL_ENRICH_SERVER_SPAN`.

spanNaming.description:
Span naming scheme.
- `"legacy"` (default): `a2a.task.execute`, `a2a.mcp.tool {tool}`.
- `"semconv"`: OpenTelemetry GenAI names, `invoke_agent {agent}` and   `execute_tool {tool}`. Only names change; attributes are identical.   The cancel span keeps its name. Migrate dashboards and queries that   match on span name before switching.

Environment override: `A2A_OTEL_SPAN_NAMING`.

taskUsageRollup.description:
Stamp per-request usage rollups (`a2a.task.usage.*`, and `gen_ai.usage.*` when the wrapper is the sole OTel source) via  {@link  applyUsageSummaryToActiveSpan  } .

Default `true` when `enabled`. Sideband `x-usage` is unaffected. Set `false` only to debug de-dupe / cardinality — rarely needed because the whole bridge is already a no-op when `enabled` is false.

OtelPropagationConfig.description: Inbound trace-context policy (same vocabulary as Elastic APM and Datadog).

carriers.description: Where to look for an inbound `traceparent`, in order of precedence: HTTP headers, then message metadata.

inbound.description:
What to do with a valid inbound `traceparent`:
- `continue`: join the caller's trace (remote parent). Connected graph.
- `restart`: start a new trace and add a span link to the caller.
- `ignore`: start a new trace and discard the caller's context.

An unauthenticated endpoint plus `continue` lets any caller choose your trace id and sampling flag; use `trustedPeers` or `restart`/`ignore` there.

trustedPeers.description: CIDRs (or single IPs) of callers trusted to supply trace context. When non-empty, callers outside the list get the `untrusted` policy. Behind a gateway also set `server.trustProxy` so the caller address is the real client.

OtelSpanConfig.description: Request-span handling relative to an existing (e.g. HTTP instrumentation) server span.

enrichServerSpan.description: In `auto`-nest, also add `a2a.*` attributes to the existing server span.

server.description:
- `auto`: if an ambient recording SERVER span exists, nest under it as an   INTERNAL child (the host already extracted the context); otherwise create   our own SERVER span and extract the caller's context.
- `own`: always create our own SERVER span and extract.
- `nest`: never extract; always a child of the active context (INTERNAL).

ProviderConfig.description:
Custom LLM provider configuration (BYOK — Bring Your Own Key).

When set, sessions use this provider instead of GitHub Copilot. Omit entirely to use the default GitHub Copilot API (no BYOK).

Supported providers and their recommended settings:

| Provider          | type        | baseUrl                                | wireApi        | |-------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------|----------------| | GitHub Copilot    | (omit)      | (omit)                                 | (omit)         | | Ollama (local)    | "openai"    | http://localhost:11434/v1              | "completions"  | | OpenAI            | "openai"    | https://api.openai.com/v1              | "responses"    | | Anthropic         | "anthropic" | https://api.anthropic.com              | (N/A)          | | Azure OpenAI      | "azure"     | https://<resource>.openai.azure.com    | "completions"  | | Azure AI Foundry  | "openai"    | https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/ | "responses" | | vLLM / LiteLLM   | "openai"    | http://<host>:<port>/v1                | "completions"  |

apiKey.description:
API key for authentication. Optional for local providers (e.g. Ollama).

Can also be set via environment variable COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY.

azure.description: Azure-specific options. Only relevant when type is "azure".

baseUrl.description:
Required. API endpoint base URL.

- OpenAI / compatible: include the full path, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1
- Ollama local: http://localhost:11434/v1
- Azure (native): just the host, e.g. https://my-resource.openai.azure.com   (do NOT append /openai/v1 — the SDK constructs the path)
- Anthropic: https://api.anthropic.com

bearerToken.description: Bearer token for authentication. Sets the Authorization header directly. Takes precedence over apiKey when both are set. Use for services that require bearer token auth instead of an API key.

type.description:
Provider type. Determines the API format and auth mechanism.

- "openai"    — OpenAI Chat Completions API and any compatible endpoint                 (Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, Azure AI Foundry, etc.)
- "azure"     — Native Azure OpenAI Service (*.openai.azure.com)
- "anthropic" — Anthropic Messages API (Claude models)

Default: "openai"

wireApi.description:
Wire API format used to communicate with the model endpoint. Only applies to "openai" and "azure" provider types. Anthropic always uses the Messages API regardless of this setting.

- "completions" (default) — Chat Completions API (/chat/completions).   Broadest model compatibility. Recommended for Ollama, vLLM, local models.
- "responses" — Responses API. Provides multi-turn state management,   tool namespacing, and reasoning support.   Recommended for OpenAI GPT-4+ and Azure AI Foundry (GPT-5 series).

advertiseHost.description: Hostname advertised in agent card URLs (default: "localhost"). Set to machine IP or "host.containers.internal" for Docker.

advertiseProtocol.description: Protocol used in advertised URLs (default: "http"). Set to "https" when the agent is deployed behind TLS or a TLS-terminating reverse proxy. The A2A spec requires HTTPS for production deployments.

cleanupInterval.description: Session cleanup interval in ms (default: 300_000 = 5 min)

idleTtl.description: Optional idle expiry in ms, measured from the last use of a context (unset by default: a context that keeps being used is only limited by `ttl`). A context unused for this long starts a new session on its next message.

reuseByContext.description: Reuse sessions by A2A contextId (default: true)

ttl.description: Maximum age of a context's Copilot session in ms (default: 3_600_000 = 1 hour). A context is resumed only while its session is younger than this, however recently it was used; after that the next message starts a new session. `0` means never reuse.

SkillConfig.description:
A single skill exposed on the agent card.

Skills describe discrete capabilities the agent advertises to orchestrators and callers via the A2A Agent Card. Each skill has a unique identifier, human-readable metadata, and optional usage examples.

description.description: Detailed description of what this skill does. Helps orchestrators decide whether to route a task to this agent.

examples.description: Optional example prompts demonstrating how to invoke this skill. Included in the agent card only when non-empty.

id.description: Unique identifier for this skill. Used as the stable key when referencing the skill programmatically.

name.description: Human-readable display name for the skill. Shown in agent card UIs and orchestrator dashboards.

tags.description: Optional tags for categorization and discovery. Orchestrators may use tags to filter or group agents by capability.

SubAgentAuthConfig.description:
Outbound credentials the bridge presents when calling a remote A2A sub-agent. Forwarded verbatim into the bridge config consumed by `a2a-mcp-skillmap`.

`mode: "none"` is equivalent to omitting the `auth` field entirely and produces no auth block in the generated bridge config.

For `mode: "api_key"`, the optional `headerName` defaults to whatever `a2a-mcp-skillmap` uses (typically `X-API-Key`).

Tokens may reference environment variables via `${VAR_NAME}` syntax; the substitution happens during validation and missing variables cause the auth block to be omitted with a warning.

SubAgentConfig.description: One remote A2A agent the parent will expose as MCP tools via the `a2a-mcp-skillmap` bridge.

agentCardUrl.description:
URL of the sub-agent's A2A agent card. Required.

Typically `https://<host>/.well-known/agent-card.json`, but any URL the bridge can probe is valid. Must use the `http:` or `https:` protocol.

auth.description:
Outbound credentials the bridge presents when calling this sub-agent. Forwarded verbatim into the bridge config.

Omitting this field is equivalent to `{ mode: "none" }`.

endpointUrlOverride.description:
Optional override for the URL the bridge probes. Useful when the agent card declares an endpoint that differs from where the agent is actually reachable (NAT, port-forward, internal vs external).

When set, this URL is passed to the bridge instead of  {@link  agentCardUrl } . The bridge still resolves a card from this URL — point it at a card URL or a base URL it can probe under `/.well-known/`. Must use the `http:` or `https:` protocol.

name.description:
Stable identifier for this sub-agent. Becomes the prefix on generated MCP tool names (`{name}__{skillId}`). Required.

Allowed characters: ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores (must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/`). Must be unique across all entries in the `subAgents.agents` array.

SubAgentsConfig.description:
Top-level shape of the `subAgents` field merged into the agent's `BaseAgentConfig`.

When this field is absent or `agents` is an empty array, the parent skips every sub-agent code path with no side effects (no bridge config written, no MCP entry injected).

agents.description: The list of remote A2A agents to expose as MCP tools.

SubAgentsOptions.description: Optional knobs that apply to the bridge process as a whole, not to any single sub-agent.

probeTimeoutMs.description: Probe timeout in milliseconds for the startup reachability check the parent performs against each sub-agent. Defaults to `5000` when unset.

responseMode.description: Skillmap response shaping mode passed through to the bridge config. Defaults to `"artifact"` when unset.

syncBudgetMs.description:
Sync budget in milliseconds passed to `a2a-mcp-skillmap` via the bridge config. Controls how long the bridge waits for an A2A agent to respond before switching to async task-handle mode.

When the budget expires the bridge immediately returns a `taskId` to the MCP client; the A2A dispatch continues in the background. The LLM can then poll via the built-in `task_result` / `task_status` tools which actively re-query the remote agent before responding.

- Set lower (e.g. `10000`) for interactive use where you want fast   task-handle responses.
- Set to `0` to wait indefinitely (no async fallback).
- Defaults to `30000` (30 s) when unset — skillmap's own default.

prompt.description: Timeout for a single prompt in ms (default: 600_000 = 10 min)

steerAck.description: How long a `steer` waits for Copilot to report how it delivered the message, in ms (default: 5_000). The report comes when Copilot consumes the message, which can be long after the send; without it the message is answered as queued by Copilot and joins the task when it starts.
